app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:118-146 — cardsFromPokemonRefs: the riskiest transformation (alternate-form exclusion, species mapping, dedup, dex sort) has zero tests
app/src/pages/index.astro:38-77 — pagination/URL-state math (page clamping, slicing, pageHref preserving filters) untested
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:294-323 — client-side table sorting incl. missing-values-last and aria-sort toggling, untested
coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests exist at all, so none of the risky logic — form filtering, pagination, sorting, URL state, 404 paths — is covered by the app's own suite.

app/src/pages/index.astro:130-176 — inline debounce/pushState/DOMParser script has no behavioural test
behaviour_not_implementation.rationale: There are no tests, behavioural or otherwise; the anchor explicitly scores 'no tests' at 1.

app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:18-56 — concurrency limiter and promise cache (acquire/release, failure eviction) are subtle async code with no regression guard
app/src/pages/pokemon/[name].astro:26-30 — only HTTP 404 is handled; any 5xx/network error crashes the whole SSR page and no test would notice
regression_power.rationale: The app's own suite is empty, so any refactor — especially of the duplicated form-exclusion logic or the client-side sort — can silently break behaviour.

evidence: app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:64-102 — the data layer is factored into pure exported functions, so a lean, high-signal unit suite would have been cheap to add
signal_to_noise.rationale: No tests means no noise, but also no signal; per the anchor, the no-tests case scores 3.

findings.issue: No test script, no runner dependency, and no test files anywhere in app/; the entire app is guarded only by the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add a lightweight runner (e.g. Vitest or node:test) with unit tests for the pure helpers in src/lib/pokeapi.js and a few Playwright smoke tests for the pages.

findings.issue: cardsFromPokemonRefs implements the trickiest logic in the app — excluding alternate forms via the species-ID set, mapping Pokémon to species, dedup, dex-order sorting — with zero tests.
findings.suggestion: Unit-test it against fixtures including ID>10000 forms, Pokémon whose name differs from its species (deoxys-normal), and null sprites.

findings.issue: Hand-rolled duplicate of the form-exclusion/dedup/species-mapping logic from pokeapi.js instead of reusing cardsFromPokemonRefs; two untested copies can drift apart (the ability page also keeps the first entry's is_hidden, ignoring later slots).
findings.suggestion: Reuse cardsFromPokemonRefs (extended with an is_hidden passthrough) and test the shared function once.

findings.issue: Pagination and URL-state math (page parsing, clamping page>totalPages, slice bounds, pageHref preserving q/type/generation while omitting page=1) is untested.
findings.suggestion: Extract the filter/paginate logic into a pure function and unit-test edge cases: page 0, page beyond the end, empty results, combined filters.

findings.issue: Client-side sortable tables (number vs text columns, '—' sorting last in both directions, aria-sort toggling across headers) are pure logic in an inline script with no regression guard beyond one acceptance test.
findings.suggestion: Extract a sortRows(rows, col, type, direction) function and unit-test it, including missing values and descending order.

findings.issue: Concurrency limiter and in-memory promise cache (acquire's while/await loop, release, eviction of failed promises) are subtle async code with no tests; a deadlock or a cached rejection would only surface under load.
findings.suggestion: Add unit tests with a controllable fake fetch covering error eviction, the waiter queue, and concurrent fan-out.

findings.issue: Only HTTP 404 is caught (same pattern in moves/[name].astro:14-19, types/[name].astro:14-19, abilities/[name].astro:11-16); any API 5xx or network error crashes the whole SSR page — an untested error path.
findings.suggestion: Add error-path tests, and consider a graceful fallback or the Not-found page for non-404 failures.

findings.issue: Inline client filter script (250 ms debounce, pushState URL sync, DOMParser #results swap, seq race guard, popstate reload) is entirely untested.
findings.suggestion: A few Playwright tests driving typing speed and back/forward navigation would pin this behaviour down.

findings.issue: Pure helpers — humanize ('mr-mime'→'Mr Mime'), dexNumber padding, latestEnglishFlavor (last English entry, whitespace collapse) — are trivially unit-testable but untested; regressions like taking the first flavor entry would slip through.
findings.suggestion: Table-driven unit tests for these helpers; they encode spec definitions verbatim.

findings.issue: Evolution chain is built by string concatenation with manual escapeHtml and rendered via set:html; a regression in escaping (XSS from API data) or nesting would be caught by nothing in app/.
findings.suggestion: Build the chain as a data structure and render it with Astro's JSX-like syntax, removing the manual escaping; test branching chains (Eevee) as data.

summary: The agent wrote no tests of its own: no test files, no runner, no test script in app/package.json:6-9, leaving the external acceptance suite as the only guard. That's a real risk here because the app concentrates subtle, refactor-hostile logic — duplicated alternate-form/species-mapping code (pokeapi.js:118-146 vs abilities/[name].astro:20-40), pagination and URL-state math, a client-side table sorter, and a hand-rolled concurrency/cache layer — much of it in pure functions that would have been cheap to test. If someone refactors the data layer, nearly every behaviour is unprotected.

untested.area: Alternate-form exclusion and Pokémon→species mapping (app/src/lib/pokeapi.js:118-146, duplicated in app/src/pages/abilities/[name].astro:20-40)
untested.likelyBug: After a refactor, Mega/regional forms (IDs >10000) reappear in 'learned by' lists, a Pokémon whose name differs from its species (deoxys-normal) links to a 404, or the duplicated ability-page copy drifts from the shared one.
Off-by-one slice bounds showing 47 or 49 cards per page, page clamping breaking on the last page, or pageHref dropping q/type/generation so 'Next page' loses the active filters.
Number columns compared as strings ('10' < '9'), '—' cells sorting first on descending, or aria-sort sticking on two headers after a click.
A deadlock when a waiter resolves after an error path, or a rejected promise being cached forever so one transient API failure permanently breaks a page.

untested.likelyBug: An API 500 or dropped connection crashes the SSR page with an unhandled exception instead of degrading; nothing exercises this path.

untested.likelyBug: A stale slow response overwriting newer results when the seq guard is broken, filters lost on back/forward, or the debounced input never firing after a refactor.
